content:
The [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Look up a domain's registration — registrar, dates, name servers. Enter your domain and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Look up a domain's registration record: who the registrar is, when the domain was created and when it expires, its name servers and its status. The data comes from RDAP, the modern replacement for WHOIS — the registry's own record, fetched live. Registrant names are usually hidden by privacy protection, and the tool shows what the record actually contains rather than guessing. The lookup runs from this site's server with strict safety limits, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the WHOIS Lookup

Start by typing or pasting your domain. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type a domain, like example.com (no http://, no path).
2. Run the lookup — the registration record appears below.
3. If no record is found, the domain may not be registered or the TLD may not publish RDAP data.

## How it works

The [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Looking up example.com shows its registrar, a 1995 registration date, its name servers and an active status — the public record, exactly as the registry publishes it. Try the same figures in the [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What the record shows

The registrar (the company the domain is registered with), the creation and expiry dates, the name servers (where the domain's DNS lives) and the domain's status codes (for example, clientTransferProhibited means transfers are locked). Registrant contact details are almost always redacted by privacy protection — that is normal, not a missing record.

## RDAP vs WHOIS

RDAP is the structured, machine-readable replacement for the old WHOIS protocol: same public registration data, in JSON instead of free text, served by the registry itself. Some country-code TLDs still do not run an RDAP service — for those, the tool reports that no data is available rather than showing a stale or invented record.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the expiry date before buying a domain — a domain expiring soon can be lost.
- Status codes like clientTransferProhibited mean the domain is locked against transfers.
- Pair this with the Domain Age Checker for the age in years and months.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a WHOIS lookup?

A query of a domain's public registration record: the registrar, creation and expiry dates, name servers and status. This tool reads it over RDAP, the modern replacement for WHOIS. Try it with your own numbers in the [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why is the owner's name hidden?

Most registrars hide registrant details behind privacy protection. The record shows what the registry publishes — usually the registrar, dates and name servers, but not the owner's name. Try it with your own numbers in the [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why is there no record for my domain?

Either the domain is not registered, or its TLD does not publish RDAP data. The tool reports that rather than guessing. Try it with your own numbers in the [WHOIS Lookup](/whois-lookup) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the WHOIS Lookup?

Just Domain. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
